skeleton: low, round Ankylosaurus like a little armoured tank on four short legs, three-quarter view turned to the left, its small head poking out from under the front of its armour: root on the ground under the body; body (pivot over the legs) with belly squash carrying, on its own bone `under` (pivot high inside the body, so it can draw up under the armour when it hides), the soft underbody (chest, tummy and hips; the throat going up under the head with a soft unoutlined top) behind the head and the armour shell (the domed back of bumpy tiles with its knobs, its front rim over the back of the head) in front of it, so the head comes out from under the armour; head (soft unoutlined back and bottom, tucked under the shell's rim and over the throat), face with eyes (the far one smaller, by the snout), brows and mouth; four short legs at the shoulders and hips, each whole to the foot: legFF and legBF (far, behind the body, shaded), legFN and legBN (near, their round outlined thighs in front of the body); foldFN/foldBN (none at rest) swap in for the near legs folded under when it lies down; tail rising behind the hips to its round club, its bone at the join (a turn swings the club side to side); hiding, the body comes down with the legs and the underbody drawn in so the armour sits on the ground like a rock and the head, scaled down at the neck, tucks in under the rim; a fern frond on its own bone at the mouth for munching.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a low, round, sand-coloured Ankylosaurus like a little armoured tank: a wide domed back covered in rounded bumpy cream tiles with small soft blunt knobs along its sides, four short legs, a tail curving up behind it to a round two-lobed club, and a small head with a rosy cheek poking out from under the front of its armour, turned a little to the left. Draw this exact Ankylosaurus as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the armour alone: the wide, low, domed back covered in its rounded bumpy cream tiles on spotted sand-brown, with the small soft blunt knobs along its sides and along its front rim, turned as in image 1, as one dome-shaped piece from its front rim (just behind the head) to its back end over the hips; without head, without legs, without tail and without the cream underside. Its front rim (where the head comes out from under it) and its bottom edge along the sides each keep their row of knobs and their dark outline, as in image 1, so the whole dome is outlined all round except at the back end: there, where the tail rises, it ends in a soft edge with NO outline (the tail tucks under it).
2. the soft body under the armour: the plump sand-and-cream chest, throat, tummy and hips that show under the armour in image 1, as one smooth rounded shape, without armour, without head, without legs and without tail: no legs, thighs or feet drawn on it, its underside one smooth outlined curve from the chest under the chin round under the tummy to the hips. At the front, the cream throat goes up as wide as it is under the head in image 1 and ends in a soft, smooth edge with NO outline (it is hidden under the head). Its whole top is a soft edge with NO outline (it is hidden under the armour). At the back, the hips run up into the very root of the tail and end there in a soft edge with NO outline across it (the tail tucks under it): no round bump, no stump, no line where the tail would join.
3. the small head alone: the rounded snout with its two little nostrils, the darker spots on top, the little soft blunt knobs on top of the head and the rosy cheek, turned as in image 1, drawn whole including the back of the head and the cheek that are normally hidden under the front rim of the armour, with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth and no mouth line; keep the nostrils, the spots, the knobs and the rosy cheek. Its dark outline runs over the top of the head, round the snout and along the jaw under the snout to the chin, as in image 1. Behind the cheek and under it (where it is hidden under the armour and runs into the throat) the head ends in a soft, smooth edge with NO outline.
4. the tail drawn whole: from its thick root (normally hidden under the back end of the armour and the hips) it curves up as in image 1, with the small rounded knobs along its top, to the big round two-lobed club at its tip; its root a soft, smooth edge cut straight across with NO outline.
5. the far front leg: the short leg on the far left of image 1, under the chin, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden behind the chest) down to its round foot with soft, round, blunt cream toenails, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
6. the near front leg: the chubby front leg in the middle-left of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its round thigh down to its round foot with soft, round, blunt cream toenails, as in image 1, the round thigh with its whole outline as in image 1.
7. the far hind leg: the darker leg partly hidden between the two near legs in image 1, drawn whole from the top of its thigh (normally hidden behind the tummy) down to its round foot with soft, round, blunt cream toenails, shaped like the near hind leg; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
8. the near hind leg: the chubby hind leg on the right of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its round thigh down to its round foot with soft, round, blunt cream toenails, as in image 1, the round thigh with its whole outline as in image 1.
9. the near front leg as when the Ankylosaurus lies down on its tummy: the same chubby front leg folded under, seen from the side, its round foot tucked forward with its soft cream toenails showing at the front; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
10. the near hind leg as when the Ankylosaurus lies down on its tummy: the same round thigh with its whole outline, the leg folded flat under it, the round foot tucked forward with its soft cream toenails showing at the front.
11. a small green fern frond for it to munch, a short stalk with a few soft leaflets, about as long as the head in image 1.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body, the armour or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no pointed claws, no pointed spikes, every knob soft and blunt. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a low, round, sand-coloured Ankylosaurus; image 2 shows the same Ankylosaurus cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the Ankylosaurus's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the Ankylosaurus in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, near the snout) is smaller than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look to the left: each big dark-brown iris sits towards the left of its cream eye, with a white sparkle in it.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a cream oval eye with a big dark-brown iris and a white sparkle, looking to the left.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, the dark-brown iris with its white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U.
4. sad: open and round, the dark-brown iris with a white sparkle, looking down and to the left, a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, to the left, the iris towards the left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1), a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, mouths, none with any teeth: 17. the mouth as it is in image 1: a thin, closed, contented smiling line, gently curved, curling up at its right end. 18. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, rounded, the inside pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth. 19. the mouth open in a small round 'o', the inside pink. 20. the mouth in a small sad frown. 21. the mouth wide open in a big round yawn, the inside pink with a little tongue, no teeth. 22. the mouth closed and chewing: a short, bunched, wavy closed line with puffed-out corners, as when munching with the mouth full. 23. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the Ankylosaurus waddles slowly along on its four short legs, its armoured back rocking gently, then stops.
the Ankylosaurus crouches, gives a tiny happy bounce off the ground and lands with a little squash.
the Ankylosaurus nods its little head yes, twice.
the Ankylosaurus shakes its little head no.
the Ankylosaurus looks one way, then the other, then back.
the Ankylosaurus laughs and laughs, its round armoured back bouncing with giggles.
the Ankylosaurus does a happy little dance, swaying from side to side, lifting its front feet in turn and swinging its club tail.
the Ankylosaurus talks, its mouth moving, its little head bobbing.
the Ankylosaurus cries, head down, little tears falling, its armoured back shaking with sobs.

the Ankylosaurus happily wags its round club tail gently from side to side.
the Ankylosaurus tucks its head and legs in under its armour and sits there like a cosy round rock, then peeks out and comes out smiling.

animations.description: the Ankylosaurus settles down on its tummy, lifts its chin up to the warm sun and closes its eyes happily, warm and cosy, then gets up again.
